8c5481c15c19.reason: The cited lines are text_of, which is only called for kind text. A file of kind file is deliberately not read as text: it is renamed to <uuid>.bin and gets its own text view (attach_docs::view), which describes a binary instead of failing. 94335c36be5d.reason: std::fs::File closes when it is dropped, including on the error path, so there is no leak. Source::open returns the BufReader or the io error and holds nothing else.

b60a9f178b47.reason: tokio::fs::write opens the file, writes it and closes it before it returns, on success and on failure, so no handle is left open. The remove_file after a failed write is the cleanup: the attachment is reported as failed to the client (who can send the file again), so the renamed .bin must not stay behind. The finding's second point, that the content is lost, is exactly that intended outcome.

ca68bdc3d179.reason: When the callback returns false, emit returns false and scan returns Ok(n) at once; the carry logic after the loop is not reached, so n is the number of lines handed to the callback, which is what the doc says (\"Returns the lines seen\"). The callers that need a total (overview, the line count of a file, the missing-line check) pass a callback that always returns true, so they scan to the end; the callers that stop early (read_page, split_parts, lines_in) use the line numbers they were given, not the return value.

da85fed55aaa.reason: The reviewer's claim is wrong in two parts: the original is not lost (it was renamed to <uuid>.bin and stays), and attach_docs::view cannot fail (every error inside it becomes text in the view; a panicked worker falls back to a plain description). But the write of the view file can fail, for example on a full disk, and then the renamed .bin stayed behind with no attachment pointing at it. keep now removes it when that write fails.

e469f93d034e.reason: The client-side name is never used as a path. The server keeps only the last path component of ?name= (rsplit on / and \) for display, stores the bytes under a generated <uuid>.<ext>, and serves them through path_for, which requires a UUID name and a known extension. A download name goes through disposition(), which drops path parts, control characters and quotes.
e469f93d034e.title: Potential Security Issue

e4795914ab81.reason: The mechanism described is not real: a line ends only at b'\\n' (CRLF included), so U+2028 and U+2029 are ordinary characters inside a line and the `ended` test cannot miss them; a multi-byte character split by a chunk is kept for the next chunk (test a_long_line_is_split_so_line_numbers_always_work). But checking the chunk boundary found a real off-by-one: a line of exactly 64 KiB, whose newline arrives alone in the next chunk, was counted with one extra blank line. scan now knows when a line continues from an earlier chunk (test a_newline_at_a_chunk_boundary_is_not_a_blank_line_and_only_newline_ends_a_line, which also covers CRLF and U+2028/2029).

f0d7788c5dfe.reason: Text is defined here as UTF-8 without NUL bytes in the first 8 KB, which is what a text reader can show; the model gets what it can read and nothing breaks if a file is oddly written. Known binary formats never take this path: a name with a reader (docx, zip, ...) stays a file, and a file with NUL bytes is binary. Test text_is_told_from_binary_by_content.

fe6620fc3b84.reason: The filename in Content-Disposition is never a filesystem path on the server: the file is read from the generated UUID path. disposition() keeps only the last component after / and \, drops control characters, quotes, ; and %, so a double-encoded %2e%2e cannot appear, and the UTF-8 form is percent-encoded. Test a_download_is_named_as_the_user_named_it covers ../../etc/pass"wd;.zip. A name of dots only now falls back to the stored name as well.
